title: assess (ax)
deck: Classroom exams from a single laptop. The teacher supervises in the terminal; students answer from any browser on the local network. No installs, no accounts, no internet.

blocks.text: Many classrooms have no stable internet, machines don't allow installing software, and creating accounts for every student takes longer than the exam itself. Online platforms assume exactly the opposite.
Then there is anti-cheat: common solutions watch through webcams or lockdown browsers, which are invasive and unfair to those who did nothing.

Everything is a single Go program. The student app (React) is built and embedded in the binary with `go:embed`; so are the SQL migrations. The teacher runs it on their laptop and students join by link, QR code or session code.

items: **The server keeps the clock.** Time does not depend on the student's device; the teacher can give extra time to one student or everyone.
**Answers survive.** They save themselves and withstand a Wi-Fi drop, a closed tab or a server restart.
**Exams as files.** An exam is a folder of YAML you can edit, copy and version.

blocks.text: `ax` only uses what a browser can see: tab switches, focus loss, copy, paste or leaving full screen. Each signal goes through a pure function that decides whether to ignore it, warn, or count a strike, depending on the chosen profile. The teacher can revert everything.

blocks.caption: Proctoring policy as a pure function: easy to test and to explain to students.

head: Profile
What it does
rows: Warns first, then counts strikes. Three strikes annul the exam.
Counts at once. The second strike annuls the exam.
